name: TIP122
description: NPN Darlington in TO-220 (TIP120/121/122 family): two transistors in one package for very high current gain, so a microcontroller pin can switch amps. Includes an internal base-emitter resistor and a collector-emitter freewheel diode. Lead order B-C-E.

TO-220.notes: TO-220, label toward you, leads down: B-C-E. Tab is the collector.

typical_application: Switching solenoids, relays, motors, and high-current LED strings directly from a 3.3V/5V logic pin. The high gain means a few mA of base current controls amps of load.
gotchas: Darlington Vce(sat) is high (~2V at high current), so it dissipates more heat than a single transistor; heatsink it
the two stacked junctions need ~1.2-1.4V base-emitter to turn on, more than a single BJT
lead order B-C-E; tab is the collector
internal flyback diode is collector-to-emitter, useful but oriented for the transistor, not a general clamp
